newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Spoornet buys into Brazil firm - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Spoornet buys into Brazil firm - paper.

text.p: South African rail transport parastatal bought a 20 percent stake of Brazilian-owned transport consortium Interferrea for an undisclosed amount, local Business Day newspaper reported on Monday.
It said the purchase was the start of an inititative to explore international joint venture opportunities in South America, the far East and sub-Saharan Africa.

Spoornet executive director Mafike Mkwanazi was quoted by the paper as saying at the weekend that Spoornet was investigating bidding for the Maputo harbour upgrade and rail rehabilitation and projects in Zambia, Angola, Cameroon and Zimbabwe.

Mkwanazi was reported as saying that Interferrea had recently bought the Malha Centro-Leste and Malha Sul rail networks totalling 14,200 km in Brazil and that Spoornet had been offered a 20 percent share in the consortium.
Spoornet had set up a firm called Spoornet Brazil with initial capital of $10 million in voting shares and a further $20 million in preferential shares represented by assets such as locomotives.
Spoornet Brazil would aim to hold equity positions in Brazilian firms to exploit operations in raiways.

Mkwanazi was also quoted as saying that Spoornet had undertaken exploratory trips to Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines. Other countries being looked at incuded Argentina, China, Chile and Pakistan.
Spoornet had also recently concluded an agreement to resume operating its trains in the new Democratic Republic of the Congo, the paper said.
It quoted Mkwanazi as saying that Spoornet was unlikely to be privatised for many years and would maintain its profitability for the year to March 1997.
